<description>
`-reindex` leaves the node unable to start when the genesis block in `blk00000.dat` has a valid header but an invalid body. With `-checkblockindex`, the default on regtest, it aborts on an assert in `CheckBlockIndex`. Without it, it stays in RPC warmup.

I stop the reindex with a fatal error when the genesis block is found invalid. Its header is already in the block index by then, so the blocks after it could not connect. A new case in `feature_reindex.py` flips a bit in the genesis block and expects the error, and on master it hits the assert instead. The reindex, loadblock, pruning and assumeutxo functional tests and the unit tests pass.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
3e65b0eaa9 validation: stop reindex on invalid genesis block

If the genesis block in blk00000.dat has an intact header but an invalid
body, -reindex adds the header to the block index and rejects the block.
The header of block 1 is then added too. With -checkblockindex, which is
on by default for regtest, CheckBlockIndex asserts that an index without
an active chain has at most one entry. Without it, the node stays in RPC
warmup.

I stop the reindex with a fatal error when the genesis block is read but
found invalid. The functional test flips a bit in the genesis block and
expects that error.
</commits>

diff --git a/src/validation.cpp b/src/validation.cpp
index 9d1e1e3563..24f4537b4d 100644
--- a/src/validation.cpp
+++ b/src/validation.cpp
@@ -5058,6 +5058,12 @@ void ChainstateManager::LoadExternalBlockFile(
                         if (state.IsError()) {
                             break;
                         }
+                        if (state.IsInvalid() && hash == params.GetConsensus().hashGenesisBlock) {
+                            // Its header is now in the block index but the block is not, so the
+                            // blocks that follow could not be connected to the chain.
+                            GetNotifications().fatalError(_("The genesis block in the block files is invalid."));
+                            break;
+                        }
                     } else if (hash != params.GetConsensus().hashGenesisBlock && pindex->nHeight % 1000 == 0) {
                         LogDebug(BCLog::REINDEX, "Block Import: already had block %s at height %d\n", hash.ToString(), pindex->nHeight);
                     }
diff --git a/test/functional/feature_reindex.py b/test/functional/feature_reindex.py
index cf45663bf0..ef4fc73684 100755
--- a/test/functional/feature_reindex.py
+++ b/test/functional/feature_reindex.py
@@ -8,10 +8,12 @@
 - Stop the node and restart it with -reindex. Verify that the node has reindexed up to block 3.
 - Stop the node and restart it with -reindex-chainstate. Verify that the node has reindexed up to block 3.
 - Verify that out-of-order blocks are correctly processed, see LoadExternalBlockFile()
+- Verify that -reindex stops with an error if the genesis block in blk00000.dat is invalid.
 """
 
 from test_framework.test_framework import BitcoinTestFramework
 from test_framework.messages import MAGIC_BYTES
+from test_framework.test_node import ErrorMatch
 from test_framework.util import (
     assert_equal,
     util_xor,
@@ -79,6 +81,28 @@ class ReindexTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         # All blocks should be accepted and processed.
         assert_equal(self.nodes[0].getblockcount(), 12)
 
+    def invalid_genesis(self):
+        node = self.nodes[0]
+        node.stop_node()
+
+        # Flip a bit in the last byte of the genesis block, the lock time of its coinbase
+        # transaction. The header stays intact, so the merkle root no longer matches.
+        # A bit flipped in the XOR-obfuscated file flips the same bit in the block.
+        blk0 = node.blocks_path / "blk00000.dat"
+        genesis_end = 8 + 285  # 8 bytes of magic and size, then the serialized block
+        with open(blk0, 'r+b') as bf:
+            bf.seek(genesis_end - 1)
+            last_byte = bf.read(1)[0]
+            bf.seek(genesis_end - 1)
+            bf.write(bytes([last_byte ^ 0x01]))
+
+        self.log.info("A reindex with an invalid genesis block stops with an error")
+        node.assert_start_raises_init_error(
+            extra_args=["-reindex"],
+            expected_msg="The genesis block in the block files is invalid.",
+            match=ErrorMatch.PARTIAL_REGEX,
+        )
+
     def continue_reindex_after_shutdown(self):
         node = self.nodes[0]
         self.generate(node, 1500)
@@ -106,6 +130,7 @@ class ReindexTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
 
         self.out_of_order()
         self.continue_reindex_after_shutdown()
+        self.invalid_genesis()
 
 
 if __name__ == '__main__':

</patch>
